podcast.title: Death from Liver Failure - 2001
podcast.body: Rockets Red Glare continued his lifestyle as a junkie, dealer, and actor until his death in 2001 from liver failure, a result of Hepatitis C. "Rockets Red Glare continued to be a junkie, a dealer, and an actor before he died of liver failure resulting from hep C in 2001."

podcast.title: Acting Career Highlights
podcast.body: As an actor, he played a taxi driver in the movie "Desperately Seeking Susan," was featured in the Eric Bogosian film "Talk Radio," played himself in the 1996 movie "Basquiat," and appeared as a barber in a 1999 episode of the HBO series "Oz." "He can be seen playing a taxi driver in the movie Desperately Seeking Susan. He was also in the Eric Bogosian film Talk Radio. He plays himself in the 1996 movie Baskwit. And if you remember the HBO series Oz, he played a barber in a 1999 episode."

podcast.title: Actor, Drug Dealer, and Key Witness
podcast.body: Rockets Red Glare was a drug dealer, bit actor, club bouncer, stand-up comedian, occasional roadie, and sometime police informant. He appeared in over 30 films, including "Desperately Seeking Susan" and "After Hours." He was called by Nancy Spungin for drugs the night she died and is a central figure in alternative theories of her murder, with some alleging he killed her during a robbery. "Let's talk about him for a second. Rockets was an actor who ended up in more than 30 films."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Sid Vicious and Questions About the Murder of Nancy Spungen

podcast.title: Alleged Involvement in Spungen's Death
podcast.body: According to a preferred theory, Rockets Red Glare, who supplied Sid and Nancy with drugs, allegedly arrived at the Chelsea Hotel between 3 and 5 AM on October 12, 1978, while Sid Vicious was unconscious. During this time, he is suspected of having stolen up to $20,000 and then murdered Nancy, whose death occurred between 5 and 9 AM. "At around 1.30 in the morning of October the 12th, Nancy called Rockets and asked him to bring some drugs. He arrived somewhere after 3 and stayed until about 5. Remember Sid is apparently completely unconscious at this point. The autopsy on Nancy suggested that she died between 5 and 9 am. The police report also says that a large amount of money was missing from the room, maybe as much as $20,000. Rockets was spotted at the hotel at around 4. There were two or three people who confirmed seeing him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Alternative Murder Suspect
podcast.body: The most popular alternative theory states that Rockets Red Glare murdered Nancy Spungin while Sid Vicious was incapacitated by drugs, in the process of robbing the couple of $1400 (and an alleged $20,000 in royalties). Author Phil Strongman's book "Pretty Vacant" advances this theory, citing Red Glare's sudden acquisition of money and new clothes shortly after Nancy's death, despite previously being broke. "The most popular alternative theory is that Nancy was killed by Rockets Red Glare."

podcast.title: Conspiracy Theory regarding Sid Vicious's Death
podcast.body: A conspiracy theory suggests Rockets Red Glare allegedly sold a super potent form of heroin to Sid's mother on February 1, 1979, knowing it would lead to Sid's overdose and death, thereby closing the murder case. "There's even a conspiracy theory that says Rockets sold Sid's mum a super potent form of heroin on 1 February 1, 1979, knowing full well that Sid would take it, OD, and die."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death and Unanswered Questions
podcast.body: Rockets Red Glare denied all accusations of murder, though he reportedly blabbed about what he did to friends and even tried to sell a snuff film of Nancy's murder. He died on May 28, 2001, from kidney failure, liver failure, cirrhosis, and Hepatitis C, exacerbated by morbid obesity, taking with him any potential answers regarding Nancy's death. "Rockets, Red Glare, died of kidney failure, liver failure, cirrhosis, and hepsi on May 28, 2001."

podcast.title: Suspected in Nancy Spungen Murder
podcast.body: Rockets Red Glare, whose real name was Michael Mora, was a New York actor and drug dealer considered the favorite suspect by many in the unsolved murder of Nancy Spungen, girlfriend of Sid Vicious. "The favorite suspect by most is a New York actor and drug dealer who went by the name Rockets Red Glare. His real name was Michael Mora, by the way."
